memory_candidates: Typst's built-in raw-block syntax highlighting applies color to fenced code even without a custom grammar; strip it via a two-pass `show raw.where(block: true)` rule (match on `it.lang == none` to avoid infinite show-rule recursion) when an austere black-only aesthetic is required.
Typst table.cell(rowspan: n) auto-skips the spanned column for continuation rows -- do not insert an extra empty `[]` placeholder cell for those rows, or content shifts out of column alignment.

Mixing `auto` and `1fr` table columns where one column has long unbreakable raw/monospace content can starve the `1fr` column to near-zero width and cause visual overlap; prefer all-fr columns with content-proportional ratios when a table has any long inline-code cells.
